title: Hire Top Talent For Your Startup With an Applicant Tracking System (July 2026)
summary: Find the best ATS for your startup this October 2026, with a comparison of pricing, features, and recruiter support options.
body_markdown:
Talent is the lifeblood of a startup, but it’s not always easy to find. There’s no magic wand to wave that will put the top candidates in front of you, ready to accept your offer. But that doesn’t mean there aren’t tools that can make the hiring process much easier, for both your hiring team and your candidates. An[applicant tracking system (ATS)](https://www.dover.com/) helps organize your hiring process and track candidates through the recruiting journey. But there are a lot of ATS options out there. How do you find the right one for your startup? In today’s article, we’ll cover some of the top ATS and recruiting tools available today, so you can narrow down your decision.


**TLDR:**


-


An ATS tracks candidates and manages your pipeline, but does not add sourcing capacity for hard-to-fill roles.


-


Paid ATS options in this roundup start from about $25 per recruiter per month, with some requiring custom quotes.


-


For senior or technical searches, a fractional recruiter can layer onto your existing ATS without rebuilding your pipeline.


-


Some tools combine free ATS software with on-demand recruiting support in a shared system, reducing coordination gaps.


-


Your best fit depends on hiring volume, role seniority, and how much recruiting bandwidth your team has available.


## Top ATS & Recruiting Software Companies


Ideally, your ATS solution gives you an all-in-one tool to manage your company’s hiring process while also fitting your budget. Here are some ATS tools for recruitment teams that could fit those parameters for your startup:

## 1. Lever


First up is Lever, which promises to help with your hiring quality and speed by way of its LeverTRM ATS + CRM system. Some top features noted by Lever include:


-


**Automation:** Custom workflows can reduce repetitive tasks when configured and monitored by your hiring team.


-


**Built-in nurturing:** Preset nurture campaign templates help you personalize outreach and may improve candidate conversion rates when messaging fits the role and audience.


-


**Actionable data:** Talent analytics give you a view of recruiting performance and hiring metrics to sharpen your strategy.


Lever’s pricing isn’t publicly listed. You can reach out for a free quote on their standard or enterprise tier.


## 2. Our Free ATS for Startups: Dover


Sure, we may be biased, but we think our ATS is one of the best solutions for startups. Here are some of our top features to help you with recruiting and hiring:


-


**AI-assisted hiring:** The free tier includes AI job description drafting. Premium adds AI resume scoring to help your team review applicants against your criteria, with hiring decisions remaining with your team.


-


**Unlimited jobs:** Post through job board integrations, with no cap on active roles.


-


**Candidate tracking:** Both plans track unlimited candidates. The free tier includes limited candidate profile and activity history; Premium includes full history.


Dover offers a free ATS tier with unlimited jobs and users, candidate tracking with limited history, job board posting, and a basic careers page. The[Premium tier costs $199/month](https://www.dover.com/pricing) and adds features including AI resume scoring, full candidate history, offer management and e-signing, and a dedicated onboarding and support call.


## 3. Ashby


Ashby is an all-in-one recruiting tool that helps companies of all sizes improve their hiring process. Some top features they call out include:


-


**One-click sourcing:** Automated sourcing emails can help build your talent pipeline and improve response rates when your team selects relevant candidates and reviews messaging.


-


**Speedy scheduling:** Interview scheduling tools can reduce setup time when interviewers keep their availability current.


-


**Easy integrations:** Connects with Gmail, Google Calendar, Slack, and other tools to keep hiring data in one place.


Ashby’s Foundations tier covers companies with up to 100 employees and starts at $400 per month. Larger teams can request a custom quote.


## 4. Zoho Recruit


Zoho Recruit is a cloud-based hiring solution that gives companies a suite of tools to hire for the roles they need. Some top features they call out include:


-


**All-in-one ATS and CRM:** Covers both applicant tracking and candidate relationship management for staffing agencies and HR teams.


-


**Automated features:** Automation tools support tasks from sourcing to communication, with your team configuring workflows and reviewing results.


-


**Advanced analytics:** Built-in reporting helps you understand and refine your recruiting process over time.


Zoho Recruit offers a basic tier with one active job for free. This limited tier comes with candidate management, interview scheduling and email management features. Paid tiers are Standard at $25 per recruiter per month and Enterprise at $50 per recruiter per month, both billed annually, per Zoho Recruit pricing.


## 5. JazzHR


JazzHR describes itself as a powerful recruiting software for small businesses. Some of the top features they call out include:


-


**Automate repetitive tasks:** Automation tools can reduce manual work when your team configures workflows and monitors candidate progress.


-


**Unlimited users:** Every plan includes unlimited users with no per-seat fees, while active job limits vary by plan.


-


**Direct integrations:** Connects with other HR tools to round out your recruiting stack.


JazzHR sells three plans at flat prices. Hero costs $1,000 per year ($110 per month if billed monthly) and covers job postings starting at 3 per month. Plus costs $3,480 per year and supports up to 200 active jobs, and Pro costs $5,508 per year and adds offers with e-signatures and advanced reporting. Some add-ons, such as candidate texting, are billed by usage. Check the JazzHR pricing page for current details.


## 6. Workable


Workable is a full-featured recruiting and management tool for hiring, onboarding, and managing team members. Some of the top features they call out include:


-


**Sourcing candidates:** One-click posting to over 200 job sites with AI-assisted sourcing built in.


-


**Automated hiring tools:** Supports approval workflows, interview scheduling, and other routine tasks, with your team retaining approval decisions and reviewing schedules.


-


**Custom onboarding:** E-signatures and employee profiles let you tailor the onboarding experience for new hires.


Workable now lists a Standard plan at $299 per month for companies with 1 to 20 employees, and pricing rises with employee count. At that same company size, Premier is $599 per month and Enterprise is $719 per month, and both include texting, video interviews, assessments, and referrals. Check[Workable pricing](https://www.workable.com/pricing) for current details.


## 7. BreezyHR


BreezyHR is a modern hiring software and ATS that works for businesses of all sizes. Some top features they call out include:


-


**Single-click sourcing:** Advertises your jobs across[50+ job sites](https://breezy.hr/attract) with one click.


-


**Task automation:** Supports pre-screening, emails, interview scheduling, and feedback collection, with your team setting criteria and reviewing results.


-


**Free templates:** HR and recruiting templates available at no extra cost.


BreezyHR offers its basic tools for one position or pool for free. Paid tiers range from $157 per month (Startup) to $439 per month (Business) when billed annually, and monthly billing costs more. A Custom Pro plan is available by quote. Check[Breezy HR pricing](https://breezy.hr/pricing) for current details.


## How Dover Stands Apart for Startup Hiring


Most ATS options on this list charge a monthly fee before you’ve made a single hire. Dover offers a free tier with unlimited jobs and users, plus a[Premium tier at $199/month](https://www.dover.com/pricing) that adds AI-assisted applicant scoring and full candidate history. You can see how it compares in our[ATS comparison for startups](https://www.dover.com/blog/best-applicant-tracking-systems-startups-top-6) .


An ATS organizes the pipeline but does not add sourcing capacity. High-volume inbound roles often run fine on an ATS alone, while senior engineering or specialized searches may call for a fractional recruiter working inside the same pipeline. Dover’s recruiter marketplace is one version of that model: recruiters set their own rates with no long-term contract, and the average cost per hire is $4,800 across all roles, though individual costs vary by role complexity. Recruiter costs are a separate budget line from ATS fees.


In a two-tool stack, a recruiter sourcing from a spreadsheet can email a candidate your hiring manager already rejected. Dover’s ATS and recruiter marketplace share one system, so your team and any fractional recruiter see the same candidate data, which can reduce duplicate outreach when both keep records current.


## FAQs


### What recruiting tools do Y Combinator startups use for hiring?


A job board shows where a startup recruits, but does not by itself identify the ATS it uses to manage applicants. YC’s[startup jobs directory](https://www.ycombinator.com/jobs/role/all) and Work at a Startup connect candidates with YC companies. For recruiting software and support,[Dover’s launch post on YC](https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/Jxh-ai-applicant-sorting-by-dover) names Scale AI, Vanta, and other startups it has helped hire. Those are documented examples of recruiting use, not confirmation of each company’s current ATS. For a founder choosing tools, candidate reach and applicant management are separate needs: a startup-focused job board can sit alongside an ATS that holds interview stages, feedback, and candidate history.


### What’s the difference between an ATS and full recruiting support?


An applicant tracking system organizes your hiring process: tracking applicants, managing stages, and storing candidate data. Full recruiting support means someone actively sourcing, screening, and managing the offer process. Most startups start with an ATS for inbound and lower-complexity hires, then add a recruiter for roles that need active pipeline-building. Some tools pair a free ATS with an on-demand recruiter marketplace in one shared system, so you can start self-serve and add human support when a search calls for it.


### Do I need a recruiter if I’m already using an ATS?


An ATS records and organizes hiring activity, but it does not source candidates, screen them, or close offers. Whether you need a recruiter on top of it usually depends on the type of role and your team’s bandwidth. Inbound-heavy, lower-complexity roles can often run on an ATS alone. Senior, technical, or specialized searches, and any search where no one on the team has hours to spare for outreach, are where a fractional recruiter typically adds capacity. The recruiter can work inside the ATS you already use, such as Ashby, Greenhouse, or Lever, or in a shared system where the recruiter and hiring team see the same pipeline. Dover’s model, a free ATS paired with on-demand fractional recruiters, is one example of the shared-system approach, with an average cost per hire of $4,800 across all roles, though costs vary by role complexity.


## Final Thoughts on Choosing the Right ATS and Recruiting Tools for Your Startup


Picking an[applicant tracking system (ATS)](https://www.dover.com/) comes down to matching the tool’s model to how your team actually hires. For high-volume inbound roles, a low-cost or free ATS with solid automation may be all you need. For technical or senior roles where inbound applicants fall short, software alone may be insufficient; active sourcing can help build a qualified pipeline. Dover is built for both situations: a free ATS plan with an optional Premium upgrade for teams that want to stay self-serve, and a recruiter marketplace for searches that need more hands-on work, all within one shared system. The right fit depends on your hiring volume, the seniority of the roles you’re filling, and how much recruiting bandwidth your team has to spare.
